# Contributing to pi-action

This document covers development setup, architecture details, and contribution guidelines for pi-action.

## Development Setup

### Prerequisites

- Node.js 24+ (LTS)
- npm

### Getting Started

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/cv/pi-action.git
cd pi-action

# Install dependencies (also sets up git hooks)
npm install

# Run tests
npm test

# Run tests with coverage
npm run coverage

# Build
npm run build

# Type check
npm run typecheck

# Run the complete quality gate
npm run check

# Run formatting and lint checks only
npm run lint

# Run dead-code and duplication analysis only
npm run analyze

# Apply safe lint/format fixes
npm run fix
```

## Git Hooks

This project uses [prek](https://github.com/j178/prek) to enforce quality checks via git hooks. Hooks are configured in [`.pre-commit-config.yaml`](.pre-commit-config.yaml) and are automatically installed when you run `npm install`.

| Hook | What it does |
|------|--------------|
| **pre-commit** | Runs fast tests and linting |
| **commit-msg** | Enforces [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format via commitlint |
| **prepare-commit-msg** | Auto-appends issue number from branch name via [`scripts/prepare-commit-msg.js`](scripts/prepare-commit-msg.js) (e.g., `feat/123-description` → `Refs #123`) |
| **pre-push** | Runs the test suite with coverage thresholds from [`vitest.config.ts`](vitest.config.ts) |

### Commit Message Format

Commits must follow the conventional commits format:

```
type(scope?): subject

body?

footer?
```

**Allowed types:** `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `perf`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`

**Examples:**
```bash
git commit -m "feat: add webhook support"
git commit -m "fix(agent): handle empty response from API"
git commit -m "docs: update installation instructions"
```

### Branch Naming

Use branch names like `feat/123-description` or `fix/456-bug-name` to automatically link commits to issues via the `prepare-commit-msg` hook.

## Architecture

The action is built with TypeScript on [pi-durable](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@earendil-works/pi-durable) and [pi-ai](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@earendil-works/pi-ai). Each issue/PR is a durable conversation whose storage is a chain of git commits on `refs/pi/threads/<number>` (the storage backend is in `src/storage/`).

### Source Files

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| [`src/index.ts`](src/index.ts) | Entry point - wires up dependencies and runs the action |
| [`src/run.ts`](src/run.ts) | Main orchestration logic |
| [`src/run-context.ts`](src/run-context.ts) | Resolving what to run on: a trigger, `pr_number`, or a direct prompt |
| [`src/thread.ts`](src/thread.ts) | One issue/PR as a durable pi conversation stored in git |
| [`src/conversation.ts`](src/conversation.ts) | Submitting triggers, waiting within the timeout, delivering each result once |
| [`src/triggers.ts`](src/triggers.ts) | Finding the `@pi` comments a thread still has to answer |
| [`src/models.ts`](src/models.ts) | Built-in providers with the `api_key` input as an in-memory credential |
| [`src/custom-provider.ts`](src/custom-provider.ts) | The single custom provider/model from the flat `provider_*`/`model_*` inputs |
| [`src/extensions.ts`](src/extensions.ts) | The `extensions` input: installing pi extensions from npm, finding their entry points, loading them with jiti, and the `pi` object they get |
| [`src/extension-provider.ts`](src/extension-provider.ts) | Turning an extension's `pi.registerProvider(name, config)` into a pi-ai provider |
| [`src/durable-extensions.ts`](src/durable-extensions.ts) | Creating the pi-durable extensions (`pi.durable`) with the run's host options |
| [`src/github-ui.ts`](src/github-ui.ts) | Questions from pi-durable extensions (`ui.ask`) as GitHub comments with checkboxes or a request for an `/answer` reply, posted without waiting; `ui.notify` in the job summary |
| [`src/answers.ts`](src/answers.ts) | Answers from the run's event (a box ticked on a question, an `/answer` reply), checked and turned into a `ui.answer` submission for the thread |
| [`src/push.ts`](src/push.ts) | The `if: always()` step that pushes unsaved thread state |
| [`src/storage/git.ts`](src/storage/git.ts) | In-process git objects and compare-and-swap ref updates |
| [`src/storage/git-storage.ts`](src/storage/git-storage.ts) | `GitStorage`: a pi-durable `Storage` whose log is a chain of commits on one ref |
| [`src/storage/sync.ts`](src/storage/sync.ts) | `GitSync`: fetching a thread ref and pushing it (fast-forward only) at turn boundaries |
| [`src/tool-env.ts`](src/tool-env.ts) | The variables the agent's tools get when the runner lacks them: `GH_TOKEN` and a `github-actions[bot]` git identity |
| [`src/github.ts`](src/github.ts) | GitHub API client helpers |
| [`src/inputs.ts`](src/inputs.ts) | Reading the action inputs (with their defaults) into `ActionInputs` |
| [`src/context.ts`](src/context.ts) | Prompt building and trigger extraction |
| [`src/security.ts`](src/security.ts) | Permission validation and input sanitization |
| [`src/formatting.ts`](src/formatting.ts) | Response formatting utilities |
| [`src/types.ts`](src/types.ts) | TypeScript type definitions |
| [`src/defaults.ts`](src/defaults.ts) | Centralized default values |
| [`src/utils.ts`](src/utils.ts) | General utility functions |
| [`src/test-helpers.ts`](src/test-helpers.ts) | Shared test utilities |

### Key Components

#### [`index.ts`](src/index.ts)
Entry point that reads GitHub Actions inputs, creates dependencies, and invokes `run()`. This is the only file with side effects (reading environment, calling APIs).

#### [`inputs.ts`](src/inputs.ts)
Reads every action input into `ActionInputs`, including the custom provider's `provider_*`/`model_*` inputs, falling back to [`defaults.ts`](src/defaults.ts) for empty or invalid values (CSV allowlists, booleans, positive integers). It takes the input reader as a parameter, so it is unit tested without loading the GitHub Actions runtime.

#### [`run.ts`](src/run.ts)
Main orchestration that:
1. Resolves the run context (trigger, `pr_number`, or direct prompt) and validates permissions
2. Sets up models from environment variables, the runtime-only `api_key` input, providers registered by pi extensions (`extensions`), and the custom provider inputs
3. Opens the thread (fetching `refs/pi/threads/<number>`; in memory for direct prompts)
4. Submits every unanswered `@pi` comment, then polls for new ones while pi works (comment mode), or runs one request (output mode, `pr_number`, direct prompts)
5. Posts each answer (or failure) once, or sets the action outputs
6. Pushes the thread

#### [`thread.ts`](src/thread.ts)
Wraps a pi-durable `Harness` on `GitStorage`:
- Fetches the thread ref, opens the conversation, resumes unfinished work
- Pushes the ref at every turn boundary (`GitSync`, fast-forward only)
- Submits comments with their GitHub ID as `requestId`, so each is answered once
- Records which results were posted, so a restarted run doesn't post them twice

#### [`github.ts`](src/github.ts)
Provides a clean interface to GitHub APIs:
- `extractTriggerInfo()`: Parses GitHub webhook payloads
- `GitHubClient`: Interface for reactions (on the issue, an issue comment, or a review comment), comments, PRs and their diffs

#### [`context.ts`](src/context.ts)
Handles prompt construction:
- `hasTrigger()`: Checks if text contains the trigger phrase
- `extractTask()`: Extracts the task from trigger text
- `buildPrompt()`: Constructs the full prompt with context
- `renderTemplate()`: Renders custom prompt templates

#### [`security.ts`](src/security.ts)
Permission and input validation:
- `validatePermissions()`: Checks the author against configured user, association, and bot allowlists
- `sanitizeInput()`: Removes HTML comments and invisible Unicode characters

### Action Configuration

The [`action.yml`](action.yml) file defines:
- Input parameters
- A composite action that:
  1. Sets up Node.js 24 if the job's Node is older
  2. Installs the runtime npm dependencies (`--omit=dev`)
  3. Installs standalone git hooks for conventional commits (see [`scripts/install-agent-hooks.js`](scripts/install-agent-hooks.js))
  4. Runs `src/index.ts` with Node's built-in TypeScript support, then `src/push.ts` in an `if: always()` step

### Testing

Tests use [Vitest](https://vitest.dev/) and are colocated with source files (`*.test.ts`).

**Running tests:**
```bash
npm test                    # Run once
npm run test:watch          # Watch mode
npm run coverage            # With coverage report
```

**Test philosophy:**
- All business logic has near-100% test coverage
- Tests use dependency injection for easy mocking
- Mock the pi SDK to test agent integration without real API calls
- Use [`test-helpers.ts`](src/test-helpers.ts) for common mock factories
- pi extensions used as fixtures live in [`test/fixtures/extensions/`](test/fixtures/extensions/); [`echo-provider`](test/fixtures/extensions/echo-provider/) registers a provider built on pi-ai's faux provider, so the `extensions` input can be tested end to end without network access; [`durable-ask`](test/fixtures/extensions/durable-ask/) is a pi-durable extension package with a tool that asks two questions the way pit does on an asynchronous host (`ui.ask`, then `ui.answer` entries on later runs)

**Coverage thresholds (enforced by pre-push hook):**
- Statements: 90%
- Lines: 90%
- Functions: 90%
- Branches: 85%

Thresholds and production coverage includes are configured in [`vitest.config.ts`](vitest.config.ts).

### Building

```bash
npm run build
```

This verifies the TypeScript production entrypoint without emitting JavaScript. Node runs the TypeScript directly (type stripping), so there is no build output and no `dist/`. That's why imports use `.ts` extensions and the code sticks to erasable syntax (no enums, namespaces, or parameter properties); `erasableSyntaxOnly` in `tsconfig.json` enforces it.

## CI/CD

### GitHub Actions Workflows

- [**CI (`ci.yml`)**](.github/workflows/ci.yml): Runs on push/PR to main - type checking, linting, and tests
- [**pi Assistant (`pi-assistant.yml`)**](.github/workflows/pi-assistant.yml): Dogfooding - uses the action from this repo to respond to `@pi` triggers

### Release Process

1. Ensure all tests pass and coverage thresholds are met
2. Update version in `package.json`
3. Create a new release/tag (e.g., `v1.0.1`)
4. Users reference the action via `cv/pi-action@v2`

## Code Style

- TypeScript with every strict compiler option on (see [`tsconfig.json`](tsconfig.json)); Node runs it directly, so only erasable syntax
- [oxlint](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter) with type-aware rules (see [`.oxlintrc.json`](.oxlintrc.json)): every rule category except the experimental `nursery` is an error, plus `typescript/no-unnecessary-condition` from it. Rules that are off are grouped with the reason they are off. Warnings fail the build, and so do `oxlint-disable` comments that no longer suppress anything
- [oxfmt](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/formatter) formats the code and JSON, and sorts imports (see [`.oxfmtrc.json`](.oxfmtrc.json)); Markdown and YAML are formatted by hand
- An `oxlint-disable-next-line <rule> -- <reason>` comment is fine when a rule is wrong for one line; put the reason after `--`
- Values from outside (JSON, GitHub payloads, git output) are `unknown` until checked, not cast

## Pull Request Guidelines

1. **Create a branch** with a descriptive name: `feat/123-description` or `fix/456-bug-name`
2. **Write tests** for any new functionality
3. **Ensure all hooks pass** - tests, type checking, linting, coverage
4. **Follow conventional commits** for your commit messages
5. **Keep changes focused** - one feature/fix per PR
6. **Update documentation** if adding new features or changing behavior

## Questions?

Open an issue or start a discussion on the repository.
# Custom Prompt Template Examples

This document provides ready-to-use custom prompt templates for various use cases.

## Available Variables

Use these placeholder variables in your custom templates:

| Variable | Description | Example |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| `{{type}}` | Context type | `issue` or `pull_request` |
| `{{type_display}}` | Human-readable type | `Issue` or `Pull Request` |
| `{{number}}` | Issue/PR number | `42` |
| `{{title}}` | Issue/PR title | `Fix login bug` |
| `{{body}}` | Issue/PR description/body | Full description text |
| `{{task}}` | Extracted task (after trigger phrase) | `please review this code` |
| `{{diff}}` | PR diff (empty for issues) | Unified diff content |
| `{{trigger_comment}}` | Full trigger comment text | `@pi please review this code` |

## Template Examples

### 1. Basic Custom Template

Simple structure modification:

```yaml
- uses: cv/pi-action@v2
  with:
    github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    prompt_template: |
      # Task for {{type_display}} #{{number}}
      
      **Title:** {{title}}
      **Task:** {{task}}
      
      ## Context
      {{body}}
      
      Please help with this request.
```

### 2. Code Review Template

Focused on pull request reviews:

```yaml
- uses: cv/pi-action@v2
  with:
    github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    prompt_template: |
      # Code Review for PR #{{number}}: {{title}}
      
      ## Description
      {{body}}
      
      ## Review Request
      {{task}}
      
      ## Changes
      ```diff
      {{diff}}
      ```
      
      ## Review Guidelines
      - Check for security vulnerabilities
      - Verify test coverage
      - Ensure code follows our style guide
      - Flag any performance concerns
      - Suggest improvements where applicable
      
      Please provide a thorough code review.
```

### 3. Minimal Template

Just the essential information:

```yaml
- uses: cv/pi-action@v2
  with:
    github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    prompt_template: |
      **Task:** {{task}}
      
      **Context:** {{title}}
      {{body}}
```

### 4. Issue Triage Template

Specialized for bug reports and feature requests:

```yaml
- uses: cv/pi-action@v2
  with:
    github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    prompt_template: |
      # {{type_display}} Triage: {{title}}
      
      ## Issue Details
      {{body}}
      
      ## Triage Request
      {{task}}
      
      ## Triage Guidelines
      - Classify the issue type (bug/feature/enhancement)
      - Assess priority and severity
      - Identify affected components
      - Suggest labels and assignees
      - Provide initial troubleshooting steps if applicable
      
      Please analyze this issue and provide triage recommendations.
```

### 5. Documentation Template

For documentation-focused assistance:

```yaml
- uses: cv/pi-action@v2
  with:
    github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    prompt_template: |
      # Documentation Task: {{title}}
      
      ## Request
      {{task}}
      
      ## Context
      {{body}}
      
      ## Documentation Standards
      - Use clear, concise language
      - Include practical examples
      - Follow our style guide
      - Ensure accessibility
      - Add cross-references where appropriate
      
      Please help improve our documentation.
```

### 6. Testing Template

Focused on test-related tasks:

```yaml
- uses: cv/pi-action@v2
  with:
    github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    prompt_template: |
      # Testing Task for {{type_display}} #{{number}}
      
      **Title:** {{title}}
      **Request:** {{task}}
      
      ## Context
      {{body}}
      
      ## Code Changes
      ```diff
      {{diff}}
      ```
      
      ## Testing Requirements
      - Write comprehensive unit tests
      - Include integration tests where needed
      - Ensure edge cases are covered
      - Follow TDD practices
      - Maintain high code coverage
      
      Please help with testing requirements.
```

### 7. Security Review Template

For security-focused reviews:

```yaml
- uses: cv/pi-action@v2
  with:
    github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    prompt_template: |
      # Security Review: {{title}}
      
      ## Security Assessment Request
      {{task}}
      
      ## Details
      {{body}}
      
      ## Code Changes
      {{diff}}
      
      ## Security Checklist
      - [ ] Input validation and sanitization
      - [ ] Authentication and authorization
      - [ ] Data encryption and secure storage
      - [ ] SQL injection prevention
      - [ ] XSS protection
      - [ ] CSRF protection
      - [ ] Dependency vulnerabilities
      - [ ] Secrets management
      
      Please conduct a thorough security review.
```

## Usage Tips

1. **Test your templates**: Start with simple templates and gradually add complexity
2. **Include context**: Even with custom templates, provide enough context for the AI
3. **Be specific**: Clear instructions lead to better results
4. **Maintain consistency**: Use similar templates across your project for consistency
5. **Version control**: Store your templates in your repository for team sharing

## Notes on Template Variables

The template system uses simple variable replacement (`{{variable}}`). It does **not** support conditional logic like `{{#if}}` or loops.

For conditional behavior (like showing diff only for PRs), consider:

1. Create separate workflow files for issues vs PRs
2. Use different templates for different event types
3. Note that `{{diff}}` will be empty for issues, so including it is harmless

## Troubleshooting

- **Variables not replaced**: Check variable names match exactly (case-sensitive)
- **Empty output**: Ensure template isn't empty or whitespace-only
- **Malformed templates**: Unknown `{{variables}}` are left as-is, not errors
- **Long templates**: No size limits, but consider readability

- Branches: 85%

Thresholds and production coverage includes are configured in [`vitest.config.ts`](vitest.config.ts).

### Building

```bash
npm run build
```

This verifies the TypeScript production entrypoint without emitting JavaScript. Node runs the TypeScript directly (type stripping), so there is no build output and no `dist/`. That's why imports use `.ts` extensions and the code sticks to erasable syntax (no enums, namespaces, or parameter properties); `erasableSyntaxOnly` in `tsconfig.json` enforces it.

## CI/CD

### GitHub Actions Workflows

- [**CI (`ci.yml`)**](.github/workflows/ci.yml): Runs on push/PR to main - type checking, linting, and tests
- [**pi Assistant (`pi-assistant.yml`)**](.github/workflows/pi-assistant.yml): Dogfooding - uses the action from this repo to respond to `@pi` triggers

### Release Process

1. Ensure all tests pass and coverage thresholds are met
2. Update version in `package.json`
3. Create a new release/tag (e.g., `v1.0.1`)
4. Users reference the action via `cv/pi-action@v2`

## Code Style

- TypeScript with every strict compiler option on (see [`tsconfig.json`](tsconfig.json)); Node runs it directly, so only erasable syntax
- [oxlint](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/linter) with type-aware rules (see [`.oxlintrc.json`](.oxlintrc.json)): every rule category except the experimental `nursery` is an error, plus `typescript/no-unnecessary-condition` from it. Rules that are off are grouped with the reason they are off. Warnings fail the build, and so do `oxlint-disable` comments that no longer suppress anything
- [oxfmt](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/formatter) formats the code and JSON, and sorts imports (see [`.oxfmtrc.json`](.oxfmtrc.json)); Markdown and YAML are formatted by hand
- An `oxlint-disable-next-line <rule> -- <reason>` comment is fine when a rule is wrong for one line; put the reason after `--`
- Values from outside (JSON, GitHub payloads, git output) are `unknown` until checked, not cast

## Pull Request Guidelines

1. **Create a branch** with a descriptive name: `feat/123-description` or `fix/456-bug-name`
2. **Write tests** for any new functionality
3. **Ensure all hooks pass** - tests, type checking, linting, coverage
4. **Follow conventional commits** for your commit messages
5. **Keep changes focused** - one feature/fix per PR
6. **Update documentation** if adding new features or changing behavior

## Questions?

Open an issue or start a discussion on the repository.

name: 'pi-action'
description: 'Run a durable pi coding agent on GitHub issues and PRs: one conversation per thread, stored in git'
author: 'Carlos Villela'
branding:
  icon: 'cpu'
  color: 'purple'

inputs:
  github_token:
    description: 'GitHub token for API access (issues, PRs, reactions, comments)'
    required: true
  api_key:
    description: 'LLM provider API key (runtime-only; alternatively set provider-specific env vars like ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)'
    required: false
  trigger_phrase:
    description: 'Phrase to trigger pi (e.g., @pi)'
    default: '@pi'
  allowed_bots:
    description: 'Comma-separated list of allowed bot usernames'
    default: ''
  allowed_users:
    description: 'Comma-separated GitHub usernames allowed to trigger pi. If set, users must be in this list.'
    default: ''
  allowed_associations:
    description: 'Comma-separated GitHub author associations allowed to trigger pi when allowed_users is empty'
    default: 'OWNER,MEMBER'
  timeout:
    description: 'Seconds before the run is aborted (its thread is still saved)'
    default: '1800'
  poll_interval:
    description: 'Seconds between checks for new comments while pi works; new trigger comments join the running conversation'
    default: '15'
  provider:
    description: 'LLM provider (anthropic, openai, google, etc.)'
    default: 'anthropic'
  model:
    description: 'Model ID'
    default: 'claude-sonnet-5-5'
  provider_base_url:
    description: 'Base URL for a single custom provider/model (e.g., https://inference-api.nvidia.com)'
    required: false
  provider_api:
    description: 'API type for the custom provider/model'
    required: false
    default: 'openai-completions'
  provider_api_key:
    description: 'Provider apiKey config value for custom providers; can be a literal key or env var name'
    required: false
  provider_auth_header:
    description: 'Add Authorization: Bearer <key> for custom provider requests'
    required: false
    default: 'false'
  model_name:
    description: 'Display name for the custom model'
    required: false
  model_reasoning:
    description: 'Whether the custom model supports reasoning/thinking'
    required: false
    default: 'false'
  model_input:
    description: 'Comma-separated custom model input modalities (text or text,image)'
    required: false
    default: 'text'
  model_context_window:
    description: 'Context window tokens for the custom model'
    required: false
    default: '128000'
  model_max_tokens:
    description: 'Max output tokens for the custom model'
    required: false
    default: '16384'
  compat_supports_developer_role:
    description: 'Whether the OpenAI-compatible custom provider supports developer role messages'
    required: false
  compat_supports_reasoning_effort:
    description: 'Whether the OpenAI-compatible custom provider supports reasoning_effort'
    required: false
  compat_force_adaptive_thinking:
    description: 'Use adaptive thinking for an Anthropic-compatible custom model (required by Claude Opus 4.6+ and Sonnet 4.6+)'
    required: false
  extensions:
    description: 'pi extensions to load: npm package specs or paths relative to the workspace, one per line or comma-separated. pi extensions contribute the model providers they register; packages with a pi-durable extension (pi.durable in package.json) add their tools to the conversation. npm packages are installed into a temp directory without lifecycle scripts. Extensions run inside the action with the job''s permissions and environment.'
    required: false
    default: ''
  trust_project:
    description: 'Let pi-durable extensions trust the repository: load and run its own configuration (such as .pi/ files). Only for repositories whose code you would run anyway; anyone who can open a PR can change those files.'
    required: false
    default: 'false'
  agent_dir:
    description: 'Agent directory (user-level state) for pi-durable extensions, relative to the workspace; a fresh temp directory under RUNNER_TEMP when empty'
    required: false
    default: ''
  prompt_template:
    description: 'Custom prompt template with placeholder variables'
    required: false
  output_mode:
    description: 'How to deliver results: comment (post to issue/PR) or output (set action outputs only)'
    required: false
    default: 'comment'
  prompt:
    description: 'Direct prompt for the agent (requires output_mode: output when no issue/PR context is available)'
    required: false
    default: ''
  pr_number:
    description: 'Pull request number to load explicitly (useful for workflow_dispatch)'
    required: false
    default: ''

outputs:
  response:
    description: 'The agent response text when output_mode is output'
    value: ${{ steps.run-pi-action.outputs.response }}
  success:
    description: 'Whether the agent succeeded (true/false) when output_mode is output'
    value: ${{ steps.run-pi-action.outputs.success }}

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    # pi-action runs its TypeScript directly, which needs Node.js 24. Reuse the job's Node when it is new enough;
    # otherwise set it up (from the runner's tool cache, so this is quick).
    - name: Check Node.js version
      id: node
      shell: bash
      run: |
        if node -e 'process.exit(Number(process.versions.node.split(".")[0]) >= 24 ? 0 : 1)' 2>/dev/null; then
          echo "ok=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        else
          echo "ok=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        fi

    - name: Set up Node.js
      if: steps.node.outputs.ok != 'true'
      uses: actions/setup-node@v6
      with:
        node-version: '24'

    - name: Install action dependencies
      shell: bash
      run: npm ci --omit=dev --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund --prefix ${{ github.action_path }}
    
    - name: Install pi-agent git hooks
      shell: bash
      run: node ${{ github.action_path }}/scripts/install-agent-hooks.js
    
    - name: Run pi-action
      id: run-pi-action
      shell: bash
      run: node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning ${{ github.action_path }}/src/index.ts
      env:
        INPUT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.github_token }}
        INPUT_API_KEY: ${{ inputs.api_key }}
        INPUT_TRIGGER_PHRASE: ${{ inputs.trigger_phrase }}
        INPUT_ALLOWED_BOTS: ${{ inputs.allowed_bots }}
        INPUT_ALLOWED_USERS: ${{ inputs.allowed_users }}
        INPUT_ALLOWED_ASSOCIATIONS: ${{ inputs.allowed_associations }}
        INPUT_TIMEOUT: ${{ inputs.timeout }}
        INPUT_POLL_INTERVAL: ${{ inputs.poll_interval }}
        INPUT_PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
        INPUT_MODEL: ${{ inputs.model }}
        INPUT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL: ${{ inputs.provider_base_url }}
        INPUT_PROVIDER_API: ${{ inputs.provider_api }}
        INPUT_PROVIDER_API_KEY: ${{ inputs.provider_api_key }}
        INPUT_PROVIDER_AUTH_HEADER: ${{ inputs.provider_auth_header }}
        INPUT_MODEL_NAME: ${{ inputs.model_name }}
        INPUT_MODEL_REASONING: ${{ inputs.model_reasoning }}
        INPUT_MODEL_INPUT: ${{ inputs.model_input }}
        INPUT_MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOW: ${{ inputs.model_context_window }}
        INPUT_MODEL_MAX_TOKENS: ${{ inputs.model_max_tokens }}
        INPUT_COMPAT_SUPPORTS_DEVELOPER_ROLE: ${{ inputs.compat_supports_developer_role }}
        INPUT_COMPAT_SUPPORTS_REASONING_EFFORT: ${{ inputs.compat_supports_reasoning_effort }}
        INPUT_COMPAT_FORCE_ADAPTIVE_THINKING: ${{ inputs.compat_force_adaptive_thinking }}
        INPUT_EXTENSIONS: ${{ inputs.extensions }}
        INPUT_TRUST_PROJECT: ${{ inputs.trust_project }}
        INPUT_AGENT_DIR: ${{ inputs.agent_dir }}
        INPUT_PROMPT_TEMPLATE: ${{ inputs.prompt_template }}
        INPUT_OUTPUT_MODE: ${{ inputs.output_mode }}
        INPUT_PROMPT: ${{ inputs.prompt }}
        INPUT_PR_NUMBER: ${{ inputs.pr_number }}

    # Pushes the thread's refs/pi/threads/<number> if the step above was cancelled, timed out, or crashed
    # before its own final push. Fast-forward only: it never overwrites another run's history.
    - name: Save pi thread state
      if: always()
      shell: bash
      run: node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning ${{ github.action_path }}/src/push.ts
      env:
        INPUT_PR_NUMBER: ${{ inputs.pr_number }}
